text: Tuesday, after the finding: the cravat recognised, Hunter recovers
why: Monday night's catastrophe is followed by Mrs. Straker waking at 1am and finding the stable and body at 7am, so the finding is Tuesday morning. Hunter's recovery and his positive identification of the cravat are both stated in ¶33–36.

text: What did the stranger want at the stable? — drug the watchman
why: Hunter states in ¶36 that the stranger drugged the curried mutton and so deprived the stables of their watchman. The question is one the story has given reason to ask, since the stranger asked about the boy and tried to bribe the maid.

text: What was in the stranger's paper? — a drug
why: The story shows the stranger holding a folded paper packet at the window, then the watchman drugged through his supper. The drug as the packet's contents is strongly implied but not explicitly stated, so this is a close call.
